items.stem: An AI model flags a claim as 'possible fraud.' How should a claims handler treat this flag?

options.text: As a prompt to investigate further, not as proof the claim is fraudulent
options.rationale: Correct: a flag indicates risk to review; it is not evidence of fraud by itself.

options.text: As conclusive proof allowing immediate denial
options.rationale: Denying on a flag alone is unfair and likely non-compliant.

options.text: As a reason to ignore the claim entirely
options.rationale: The claim must still be handled; the flag prompts review.

options.text: As irrelevant, since fraud flags are never useful
options.rationale: Flags can usefully focus review when treated as signals, not verdicts.

items.explanation: Correct: a flag indicates risk to review; it is not evidence of fraud by itself.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO practices support responsible AI-assisted claims triage? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Having an authorised handler make the final coverage decision
options.rationale: Correct: coverage decisions must rest with an authorised human.

options.text: Handling claimant personal data in line with privacy rules
options.rationale: Correct: privacy duties apply to personal data used by claims AI.

options.text: Auto-declining any claim the model scores as high risk
options.rationale: Automated declines on a score alone are unfair and risky.

options.text: Sharing full claim files with any external tool for convenience

items.explanation: Correct: coverage decisions must rest with an authorised human.

items.stem: An AI summary says a claim is 'covered under the policy.' Before acting, what should the handler verify?

options.text: The stated coverage against the actual policy wording and endorsements
options.rationale: Correct: coverage statements must be checked against the governing policy document.

options.text: Nothing; AI coverage statements are always correct
options.rationale: AI can misread policy terms; verification is needed.
The coverage position itself is what must be verified.

options.text: That the summary is long enough
options.rationale: Length is irrelevant to whether coverage is correctly stated.

items.explanation: Correct: coverage statements must be checked against the governing policy document.
